issues.description: The middle and little fingers' joints bend sideways in 3D. Interphalangeal joints are hinges, so this is anatomically impossible. This calibration run introduced it, the report does not mention it, and a pose edit fixes it within every gate. Against each finger's MCP flexion axis: the middle DIP bend of 50 deg is ~49 deg sideways (only ~7 deg is flexion). The little finger's PIP bend of 55 deg is ~50 deg sideways and its DIP bend of 63 deg is ~62 deg sideways; the two bend in nearly opposite senses (dihedral about the PIP-DIP bone 153 deg, where 0 = a same-sense curl), so the finger zigzags. The middle fingertip lies 9.8 mm off the plane of its first three joints. The ring's PIP/DIP stay coplanar with each other (dihedral 4.5 deg) but sit ~40 deg off its MCP flexion axis (~20 deg sideways at the PIP). The pre-step-2 pose had <= 5 deg sideways at every interphalangeal joint. The cause is the new depth rule, 'solve z from target bone lengths, and keep a bone at its parent's depth when its projection is already too long' (pinky_pip and pinky_dip both at z -0.0009; middle_dip and middle_tip both at 0.254). Nothing in that rule keeps a finger in one flexion plane. The report says the depths were solved from anatomical bone lengths and calls the anatomy plausible. The kinks are invisible from the home camera and subtle in the check views (in yawm35 the middle reads as a DIP-only hook with a straight PIP; from above, the little finger's middle phalanx runs sideways), and obvious from the fingertips or the palm side, i.e. once the camera moves. Fixable within every gate. X5 (little finger only: pinky_pip px (969,686) z -0.016, pinky_dip px (977,719) z 0.043, pinky_tip z 0.102) passes every gate: IoU 0.9296, mean 3.428, p95 7.616, negative space 0.8683, pinky tip 3.16 px (was 4.24), pinky joints 1.43-1.75 u. Its bones are 32.6/18.2/18.8 mm (target 33/18/19) and its PIP/DIP bends are 27/10 deg flexion with <= 2 deg sideways. X8 (X5 plus middle_pip z 0.143, middle_dip px (851,614) z 0.218, middle_tip z 0.299) passes every gate: IoU 0.9264, mean 3.581, p95 8.246, negative space 0.8554, tips 1.0/2.24/2.24/3.16 px, all 16 joints <= 1.82 u (middle_dip now 0.53 u), 0 mask holes, A1 and D9 unchanged, no new interpenetration. There the middle DIP bends 23 deg in flexion and 10 deg sideways, with bones 40.3/29.1/28.6 mm. X8 costs silhouette margin (the pinky now sits 5-7 px left of the reference instead of 3-5 px right; the middle tip is 3-4 px low), so a fixer should tune between them. If no planar solution keeps every gate, the anatomy-versus-pixels trade goes to the user.

issues.description: A dorsal knob and notch that neither the residual list nor the open issues mention. From the home camera, a rounded knob (the carpus capsule's end cap, Seg(wrist, palm) with a cap only Np = Ap*flat long) stands above the index-metacarpal line, with a sharp concave crease in front of it at about (1085-1120, 533-545). The step-2 palm change (r 64 -> 102, flat 0.45 -> 0.30) made it prominent; before step 2 it was only a small ledge. The render's top outline is 7-11 px below the reference at x 1050-1095 (543 against 532 at x 1085) and 8-10 px above it at x 1130-1160. This is the third-largest cluster of edge errors over 8 px (render->ref 12.0 px, ref->render 10.3 px). It is also visible in yawm35 and would show in the app's solid mode. The pose can soften it but not remove it. X3 (palm flat 0.45) improves every silhouette metric (IoU 0.9323, mean 3.305, p95 7.280) and halves the notch, at the cost of the thicker 3D palm the calibrator chose to avoid. X2 (palm px (1075,633)) fills the notch and passes, with p95 8.246. X1 (palm lowered, r 98) deepens it and fails p95 and D9. It belongs in the residual list and in the step-3 palm-form builder request.

An unreported wrist collar. Where the forearm segment and the carpus segment meet at the wrist joint, there is a raised ring. The two segments solve their wrist sections separately along different axes (32 deg and 20.6 deg in the image). It shows in yawp35, yawm35 and above, and faintly from the home camera at about (1292-1317, 645-660), just inside the scored region. The report only mentions the separate off-frame forearm cuff. It belongs with the step-3 cuff fix.
